edges.description: Reduced brain and eye size and a small cerebellum, with reduced motor response to light.
edges.limitations: Reduction in overall brain size is not specific to the cerebellum, and the zebrafish phenotype is embryonic rather than the postnatal-onset atrophy seen in one patient.

nodes.description: Cerebellar ataxia with limb tremor, first noted at 4 years, in the second individual; not assessed in the first.

evidence.reference_title: LSM7 variants involving key amino acids for LSM complex function cause a neurodevelopmental disorder with leukodystrophy and cerebellar atrophy.
evidence.snippet: Neurological features found during his clinical examination included axial hypotonia, postural instability, spasticity of the four limbs, extrapyramidal dyskinesia, and cerebellar features such as nystagmus, oculomotor apraxia, tremors of the limbs, and ataxia.

evidence.reference_title: LSM7 variants involving key amino acids for LSM complex function cause a neurodevelopmental disorder with leukodystrophy and cerebellar atrophy.

nodes.description: Biallelic missense variants at Asp41 (an RNA-contacting Sm motif I residue) or Arg69 (an LSM5-contacting residue) reduce LSM7 abundance and its ability to bind its ring partners. LSM7 is a core subunit of LSM2-8, the U6 snRNP component of the spliceosome, which is the basis for conformance to the spliceosome module; LSM7 is equally a subunit of the non-spliceosomal LSM1-7 decay complex. Patient fibroblasts carrying homozygous p.Asp41Asn have reduced LSM7 mRNA and protein.

nodes.description: In HEK293 affinity purification-mass spectrometry, FLAG-tagged LSM7 p.Asp41Asn and p.Arg69Pro co-purify far less of the other LSM subunits of both rings than wild-type LSM7, and lose most known interactors of both complexes. This is the only molecular defect demonstrated so far; it does not distinguish which ring's loss is pathogenic.
